purpose: Recall-keyed product-level ledger showing a 2025 repair route followed by a 2026 expansion stating that the previous repair was ineffective, while preserving the purchaser-level recovery gap.

events.geography: United States; Sauna360 Tylö Halmstad and Kiruna Hybrid sauna rooms
events.denominator: About 1,000 sauna rooms; not unique owners or households
events.method: Structured extraction from the official CPSC recall notice for recall 26-040
events.missingness: Owner notice, possession, appointment, repair completion, downtime, safe use, and later owner outcome are not observed
events.exposure: Bench seating could break and create a fall hazard; CPSC reports seven breakage reports, including one head-and-neck injury
events.alternatives_before_action: An owner could stop using the bench, contact Sauna360, schedule the free repair, use another facility, or continue use; the notice does not observe the choice
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: A free professional repair and revised manual are offered, while scheduling, access, and downtime costs are unmeasured
events.choice_or_response: Sauna360 offers additional hardware installation and a revised weight-limit manual through a professional installer
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Sauna360 and its installer control repair execution; CPSC controls the public recall notice; owners control action after receiving usable notice
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: CPSC publishes a recall and Sauna360 offers a free repair
events.durability_followup: A later recall expansion reports the earlier repair was ineffective
events.immediate_outcome: A dated hazard and first repair route are publicly identifiable
events.protected_outcome: Potential fall risk may be reduced by a completed repair; safe restoration is not observed
events.sacrificed_outcome: Use, recreation, time, mobility, and possible substitute costs may be sacrificed but are not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: Owners may bear notice, scheduling, access, and downtime burdens while the firm executes the repair
events.later_outcome: A later official expansion states that the previous repair was ineffective; this event alone does not establish failure on every unit
events.meaning_and_attribution: No owner-level fairness, blame, trust, or identity judgment is measured
events.public_or_collective_response: The public recall system supplies notice and instructions; no owner complaint, appeal, or collective response is linked
events.counterexample: A repair offer and incident report do not establish owner receipt, repair need, or completed safe use
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official CPSC recall notice dated October 23, 2025; reported unit and incident figures are notice-level counts, not unique-owner rates

events.geography: United States; Sauna360 Tylö Halmstad and Kiruna Hybrid sauna rooms
events.denominator: About 6,000 sauna rooms; includes products covered by the earlier recall and is not a unique-owner denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official CPSC recall-expansion notice for recall 26-783
events.missingness: No owner list, first-repair receipt, second-notice receipt, appointment, second-repair completion, downtime, substitute access, residual loss, or later trust/behavior is observed
events.exposure: The notice says the previous repair was ineffective and reports 77 additional breakage reports, including six injuries
events.alternatives_before_action: An owner could stop using the sauna, contact Sauna360 for the second repair, seek another installer, use a substitute, or continue use; owner choices are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Owners are told to stop using the product even if they received the 2025 remedy; a second free professional retrofit is offered
events.choice_or_response: CPSC expands the recall and Sauna360 offers additional hardware and professional installation
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Sauna360 and its installer control the second repair; CPSC controls public communication; owners control response after notice
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: A repeat-remedy route is issued after the earlier repair is described as ineffective
events.durability_followup: Second professional repair is offered; completion and later safe use are not observed
events.immediate_outcome: A dated remedy-durability failure and second repair route become publicly observable
events.protected_outcome: A second repair may reduce fall risk; completion and safe restoration remain unobserved
events.sacrificed_outcome: Prior repair effort may have failed to provide durable safety; downtime, cost, and access effects are not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: Repeat notice, scheduling, interruption, and verification burdens may fall on owners while the firm executes the second retrofit
events.later_outcome: The remedy chain advances from first repair to reported ineffectiveness and second repair, but no purchaser-level completion or recovery endpoint is available
events.meaning_and_attribution: No owner-level trust, fairness, blame, or switching response is measured
events.public_or_collective_response: The CPSC recall system records the expanded remedy; no owner-level complaint or collective action is linked
events.counterexample: A repeat recall demonstrates remedy failure at the institutional/product level, not that every owner experienced the same failure or that the second remedy will fail
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official CPSC recall expansion dated September 17, 2026; reported incidents and unit counts are not unique-owner estimates

arrows.to: first public recall and professional repair
arrows.evidence: The October 2025 CPSC notice identifies the hazard and offers a free professional repair with additional hardware
arrows.counterexample: An offered repair is not a completed repair or safe restoration
arrows.remaining_gap: Owner notice, appointment, repair receipt, and safe use

arrows.to: reported ineffective repair and expanded recall
arrows.evidence: The September 2026 CPSC expansion states that the previous recall repair was ineffective and reports additional breakage and injuries
arrows.counterexample: The notice does not establish that every first repair failed or identify the repaired units among the reports
arrows.remaining_gap: Repair-level denominator, failure mechanism, owner receipt, and timing

arrows.evidence: The expansion instructs owners to stop use even if they received the 2025 remedy and contact Sauna360 for another free repair
arrows.counterexample: A second offer is not a completed retrofit or proof of durable safety
arrows.remaining_gap: Second notice, scheduling, installation, completion, and follow-up inspection

arrows.to: safe use, household security, trust, or exit
arrows.evidence: No purchaser-level notice, repair receipt, downtime, substitute access, safe-use outcome, trust, switching, or exit is in the public record reviewed
arrows.counterexample: Institutional correction can occur while an owner remains uninformed, delayed, or unable to use the installer route
arrows.remaining_gap: Lawful owner-level notice, repair completion, residual cost, safe restoration, attribution, trust, and behavior follow-up

boundary: This ledger records a product-level hazard, first repair, reported remedy ineffectiveness, and second repair route. It does not estimate purchaser exposure, notice, repair completion, safe restoration, trust, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: No owner file, raw complaint, raw CPSC response, direct identifier, or installer record is retained; only compact derived fields, public source references, and open arrows are represented.
